name: Voiden Tool
description: Mark an existing request as a named, typed capability an AI agent can call directly — instead of only the four generic run/list/write tools every project gets by default.
author: Voiden Team
readme: Tool declaration extension. Insert a /tool block on an existing request block, fill in its agent-facing identity (name, description, annotations), declare which parameters the agent controls vs which come from the environment, and list which other requests verify it still works. Verified tools are served as real, individually-named/typed MCP tools by @voiden/mcp and voiden-runner mcp serve, alongside the four generic run/list/write ones every project gets by default — with a manual enabled override (add/remove from serving regardless of verification state) available in the block's own attrs.

blocks.description: Owns 3 block types for tool identity, parameters, and verification policy

features: Declare an existing request as a named, described, agent-callable tool
Parameters table with agent-supplied vs environment-only (resolved from the project's env files, never sent to the agent) sources
Verification policy referencing other requests as happy-path/error-contract/auth-check proof the tool works, each with its own live/sandbox/none mode and optional cadence
Per-request onFailure policy — each verification request decides its own consequence (withdraw the tool, or keep it flagged degraded); the most conservative failed one wins when they disagree
Dynamic MCP serving — verified tools become real, named/typed tools in @voiden/mcp and voiden-runner mcp serve, alongside the 4 built-in ones
Manual enabled override — add or remove a tool from what's served regardless of its verification state
voiden-runner tool list / tool verify — project-wide discovery and pass/fail verification from the CLI
voiden-runner mcp serve --check — reports served/withdrawn/degraded/excluded without starting a live session
Cross-file request/verify references save a portable relative path, resolved against the referencing file's own project
